item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Hey. EponymousRex. Occasionally go by SteelGriffin or Griff sometimes. Long time reader, first time proper official poster. Heh, fiddled around with discussion the old IRC a fair number of years ago. Wanted to write someone/something as a comical doom magnet. Some poor dude attracting suffering enough to make him hate his pitiful existence, but never enough to end it. As if that hasn't been done to death, and honestly I'm surprised I remember it. Oh well.

I might try to do something more than read and so on, but probably not for awhile. Not until I'm over my anxiety and general cowardice.

I always found the Idea beyond the SCP setting, and the general mechanics of it as a collectively written universe to be fascinating. A massive cooperative writing project that has produced something so wonderful and thought provoking, not to mention Fun. So not only am I here for the stories, I'm here to watch the community, and I'm kicking myself for not deciding to become involved sooner.

Anyway to answer the question prompt. Despite my previous noting on my own anxieties, that rarely keeps me up that much. It's more just… My mind gets going on some idea, some story, some THING I want to write, create, etc. Though I do worry. About Family, about the future, all that crap. You know how it is.

Hello everyone, I am very grateful to be a part of this site. I first discovered SCP when I saw a new uploaded video on Youtube at the time SCP-087 in very early 2012. My hobbies are listening to music, watching anime, and playing video games.

As for the question, my answer is: Embarrassing things I did when I was a kid.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Jabobai! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's great to see you are as fascinated with the SCP Universe as we are here on-site. Hopefully your future readings won't disappoint you and will only make the feeling of wonder even greater. It also seems like you really want to contribute to the site, which I am very happy for; I can't wait to see what you come up with!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hey all. My name's John, and I'm a teenager living in Michigan, USA.

I've known about the Foundation for years now, and it's been long enough that I don't remember exactly how I discovered it, although it was probably through watching Let's Plays of Containment Breach back in the day. This community seems like a welcoming place, but I'm not quite sure what I want to do here, whether it be writing SCPs or just reading and giving my input.

In real life, I like learning about history and government, and just researching things in general. More recently, I've started to get into graphic design and perhaps even architecture, which seems like a good career to go into.

What keeps me up at night is mostly my imagination. I usually either place myself in fictional scenarios, or use fictional characters to carry out said scenarios. These scenarios I create usually revolve around something that interests me or whatever occupied my time that day. Hopefully I can utilize my creativity and put it to good use here.

I'm glad to be finally joining the site after all these years, and I'm looking forward to contributing to the community.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone! I'm Ross - although you can call me Mira too, if you'd like!

I'm 20 years old, and I've been been a casual reader of SCP articles for what must be almost five or six years now. Recently, though, I've delved far deeper into the assorted canons and some of the less "popular" articles, and I'm amazed by just how much the site really has to offer.

I enjoy the tone of the SCP Wiki on the whole - the general style is one that I am not particularly good at writing, but enjoy reading to a great extent. The creativity on display in exploring concepts from the harmlessly light-hearted to the ones so horrifying that they have stuck with me for years is nothing short of admirable. (Perhaps one day, I'll workshop an idea of my own, but that isn't likely to happen for a very long time.)

As far as hobbies go, I enjoy character design and writing, and as some have likely deduced from my username, I'm a huge fan of visual novels as well. I also like baking, although most baked goods tend to be a little too sweet for my personal tastes.

With regards to what kind of random thoughts keep me up at night, they tend to range from something as mundane as having a song stuck in my head to whatever catastrophic situations my tired, anxious mind is able to come up with. Typically, though, they'll just jump from one topic of interest to another - usually if I've read something I really enjoyed, I won't be able to stop thinking about it.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hi there, I'm Luggy.
I haven't posted on here in years so I thought I may as well re-introduce myself.

I discovered SCP a long time ago through the numerous fan-games that it spawned. Back then, I joined the site to improve my English and try to write for the site. However, I was also a teen who had no idea of what he was doing, so that didn't go very far. It's only recently that I rediscovered the site thanks to channels like TheVolgun and The Exploring Series and it has renewed my love for the site.

Writing an SCP when you're 17 sounds great, but now that I'm older, my goals have changed. I just want to hang out here and maybe improve my writing while I'm at it. If you guys got any suggestions regarding the latter, I'd love to hear them.

As far as hobbies go, my main hobby is drawing. I'm not great at it, but it's still something I'm passionate about. You can check out my art on Newgrounds.
Despite being an English major (in France), I still need to read more. Forcing people to read books you don't care about does that to you.

What kind of random thoughts keep me up at night ? Most likely all my old posts on here that have been buried by time. Crazy how a person can change in a few years.

Hoping I'll hang out longer here. Cheers !

Hello DeltaThree,
My name is metaldragonx1,
I would.like to say welcome to the SCP Wiki. I'm new to the site as well, but I've being whatever I can to help the community grow.

I strongely advise you post any idea on the ideas section of the forum and get a greenlight (per SCP wiki policies before you can move forward on this new character, but in the meantime, you can try to make it the best SCP it could be. When you post it, you can receive the critique needed. When you get greenlit from 2 authors (also per policy), then you can work on the sandbox and get further critique before you can make it an SCP.

I'm not qualified to do greenlights, but I can still critique certain works.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi all!

I found out about SCPs first on YouTube, where I first seen video about the SCP-173.
And there it escalated to 001 - When day breaks, 049 - the plague doctor, 096 - The shy guy and 106 - The old man.
Then I discovered that there is a game, SCP: Contaiment breach.
But that game wasn't fun for me because scp-106 and the fact that its horror game.
(Well I had fun when I turned on godmode and I played with peanut but thats for another topic.)
Then I found this site, the SCP wiki!
But my "ideas level" was at zero so I mainly only read scps.
Then I found another game, SCP: Secret lab.
I have at least fun in that game since is not that scary as scp:cb.
And im not hating on scp:cb Its just not my cup of tea.
Well I can say that SCP: SL put my "ideas level" to 10… and I wanted to write some scps.
So here I am! Ready to write some SCPs for the site.
Thanks to covid my hobby is… Well… Not existing.
So im looking into this as my new hobby.

The last thing that I can say is
Merry christmas!

(Also they should nerf 096 in secret lab. Im just sayin.)

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, I actually jojned last month, but it took this long to figure out the work around for Chrome. Now that I'm here I have a few ideas, some are random SCP articles(which I will provide a brief list of in order to get feedback on which one you'd like to see first) and I want to introduce an OC to lay the groundwork for a movie and TV series. The OC is not going to be it's own SCP, rather it will be adapted from SCP-2806, specifically an arm that can double force/strength and has a retractable aramid covering. The individual this is attached to, SCP-2806-21A, is permitted to keep the arm in exchange for working for the Foundation as a member of MTF Alpha-9, an offer made when it managed to survive a security breach involving SCP-682 and actually helped recontain it. I need to figure out how to add an addendum to put this in, unless someone can explain the process better to me. The SCP article addendum would only include a description of the new instance, updated containment procedures and an interview between SCP-2806-21A and the agent that brought him in, other details will follow in tales that would connect to the Ressurection Canon, and by the nature of SCP-2806, create crossover with Those Twisted Pines.

– hide block

Also I'd like to add to SCP-2923, Electric Lemonade flavor, the D-Class is now being used to power Site [REDACTED]

SPC-2806: cybernetics for pugilists who lost limbs in shark attacks so that they may once again punch sharks.

Other fun SCP ideas:
Playing with Fire - silly putty like substance that is plasma at room temperature, from Dr. Wondertainment.
Vampire Bodega - mini-mart where everything seems to be free, but actually draws blood from customers, not noticeable unless the customer comes more than twice a week. May be part of Marshall, Carter and Dark.
Cryovampire - cryogenically preserved person who was successfully revived, but now absorbs heat energy. Must be kept in a room heated to 98.6 degrees Farenheit at which point the ambient temperature neutralizes the anomaly, but as soon as it is exposed to lower temperatures it reverts to a savage that freezes anything it touches.
Alzoidian - a cephalopod like alien life form native to the red spot of Jupiter. Exists in symbiosis with a fungus and another species that resembles a manta ray. Still not quite sure how to explain how the foundation even acquired it…
Scapegoats - the acursed goats that carry the sins of the nation of Israel according to an ancient ritual.
Swine Legion - the accursed swine possessed by demons exorcised by Jesus.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
